key_insight: The paper shows that quantum circuit expressibility is only meaningful when it is supported by enough measurement samples, leading to an adaptive sample-supported notion of circuit complexity.
engineering_relevance: For practical quantum machine learning, it provides a principled way to choose ansatz size based on available data instead of fixing circuit depth by hand.
method: Derive an information-theoretic Occam bound for pure states generated by at most G two-qubit gates.
Define best G-gate approximation error d_G(ρ̂) and approximate circuit complexity Cη(ρ̂) for arbitrary quantum sources.
Prove an adaptive model-selection theorem that selects circuit complexity from data without knowing G in advance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports matching upper and lower bounds, including a sample-supported expressibility law M ≳ G/ε² up to logarithmic factors and saturation near 2^n.
watch_item: The guarantee is asymptotic and subject to tomography saturation, so gains may be limited for large n or when sample counts are too small to resolve higher-complexity circuits.
paper_title: Quantum Occam Learning: Sample-Supported Expressibility for Circuit-Based Quantum Learning
